correctness.rationale: The exact inverse Hessians follow by rank-one eigenspace inversion. Equation (3) is positive semidefinite termwise under mN<=Q<=MN, yielding H_Q<=KH_N and exact K from the two-coordinate near-axis limit. If K<=1, convexity plus coordinate-monotonicity of the squared positive-orthant defect gives an absolute norm and then the Banach-block triangle inequality. If K>1, the sharp near-axis Hessian ratio produces a negative second derivative of any alleged squared norm. A zero and a positive multiplier give an explicit small-epsilon midpoint violation. Positive definiteness follows M<1. Sympy p=4 2D inversion identities and 5250 deterministic numerical checks corroborate the analytic proof, not substitute for it.

value.rationale: The criterion computes a complete natural continuous-parameter phase region of positive nonconstant diagonal strict contractions in super-Hilbert ell_p geometry, revealing admissible non-Hilbert single-operator dilations absent in zero-band families. The exact sharp n-dimensional Hessian comparison explains the phenomenon structurally, gives a natural quantitative curvature invariant, and makes the critical equality and zero-weight boundary explicit. It answers a parameter-classification gap motivated by the 2026 defect condition, not merely a trivial special case or a finite calculation.
